summary:
On Tuesday we received Locus and saw that we are supposed to get married this week. So we did. 

We got married yesterday, here in our apartment, with lots of flowers and Mumm’s champaigne and then Tessa’s father took us out to dinner (I had veal Oscar which cost $8.50. Tessa had an open faced peanut butter sandwich and a glass of chilled Chenin Blanc, Wenti Bros.). This morning when I opened the apartment door I found a great bunch of lovely flowers that Linda had brought in the night. Wow. 

Otherwise, things are pretty routine. 

As I guess I told you, Doubleday did accept FLOW MY TEARS. Also, I fin­ ished the rough draft of A SCANNER DARKLY. 320 pages written in less than two months. 

Now I am resting. 

See? Very short paragraphs. 

 2i 

Hmmm. 

Oh well. Gobye, Sherry. Sigh. (Zzzzzzzzzzz.) 

 Mrs. Phil Pinky 

P.S. God sent us a wedding present. In the middle of the night last night there was a terrible cat fight, and when we got up this morning and looked out, there in the gutter dead lay Pinky’s nemesis, the huge Siamese who even attacked Tessa one time. Evidently he attacked a passing car, rather than yielding the rightaway. 

ITO CAROL & TERRY CARR] 

Did Bob and Barbara mention to you, by any chance, that we got mar­ ried? (I mean Tessa and I, I mean.) I’m hoping they did mention it, because we were wondering if maybe you and everybody else might want to send us money and presents and things such as best wishes.
